title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is building a formalism for the 'structure at infinity' of moduli spaces M_{g,ν}. The boundary of the stable compactification is a normal crossings divisor in the orbifold or stack sense, and its components may self-intersect.

The set-up on the previous page:
- X = D_0 is a space.
- For each d there is a local immersion i_d: D_d → X, of codimension d. D_d is the normalized locus of points lying on at least d branches.
- D_d^! → D_d is an étale S_d-torsor that orders the d local branches.
- For x ∈ D_d, the set I_x of lifts of x to D_{d,1} (over D_1) has cardinality d. Its elements give sections s_i, and the images of the s_i are germs x_i in D_1.

On this page:
1. The d points x_i define d germs of smooth hypersurfaces D_x^i in X at a = i_d(x). Each contains the germ of D_d at x.
2. Axiom: the germ (D_d, x) → (X, a) is the intersection of the D_x^i, and the intersection is transversal. This is the usual local normal-crossings condition, phrased intrinsically via the system (D_d, D_d^!, D_{d,d'}) rather than via a divisor.
3. Example: X = D_0 a plane, D_1 the normalization of a drawn curve (a nodal curve; a second figure shows another self-crossing curve), D_2 the crossing locus. The text states that such a situation 'cannot be described by the datum of a divisor on X'. Presumably he means a divisor with strict normal crossings, i.e. a sum of smooth components: the branches are only locally distinguishable, and globally there is monodromy permuting them.
4. Construction (183): the permutation action of S_d on Z^d, twisted by the torsor D_d^!, gives a local system of free Z-modules of rank d, T_d = D_d^! ∧^{S_d} Z^d, on D_d.
5. Construction (184): G_d = T_d ⊗_Z G_m = D_d^! ∧^{S_d} G_m^d. This is a relative torus (analytic or algebraic) over D_d, a twisted form of G_m^d.
6. Interpretation (last line): T_d is the local system of π_1 = H_1 of the fibres of the deleted tubular neighbourhood of D_d. Those fibres are homotopic to (S^1)^d. In the moduli context these are the lattices generated by the Dehn twists about the d vanishing cycles.
7. Next page: the conormal line bundle L_1 of D_1 → X is pulled back by the s_i to bundles L_{d,i}. The product of their G_m-torsors is a G_m^d-torsor P_d^! on D_d^!. It is S_d-equivariant, so it descends to a G_d-torsor P_d on D_d. P_d models the punctured normal bundle (the deleted tubular neighbourhood) of the stratum.

Purpose: an intrinsic description of the 'tubes' around boundary strata, and of their local monodromy tori, for M_{g,ν} at infinity.
errors: Mild imprecision: a plane nodal curve IS a (Cartier) divisor on X. What cannot be given is a strict normal crossings divisor, i.e. a sum of smooth components. The data D_d, D_d^! encode the self-intersection that a mere divisor does not keep in a usable form. (In the stack setting for M_{g,ν} the statement is more substantively true.)
The marginal note 'D_2 = ∅' (if read correctly) would be wrong for the nodal-curve figure, where D_2 is the node. It may refer to a different figure, or be a misreading.

ideas.what: Encoding a normal crossings situation by a hierarchy of local immersions D_d → X, plus S_d-torsors D_d^! ordering the branches, with a transversality axiom
ideas.modern_name: Normalization of the d-fold locus of a normal crossings divisor; stratification with branch-ordering torsors
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne, Théorie de Hodge II (1971): normalizations of d-fold points and their orientation local systems ε^d; standard in log geometry

ideas.what: Local system T_d = D_d^! ∧^{S_d} Z^d and relative torus G_d = T_d ⊗ G_m
ideas.modern_name: Twisted torus of the stratum; relative version of the log/monodromy torus (cf. Kato–Nakayama fibres (S^1)^d, the group of Dehn multitwists)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Deligne (Hodge II), Kato–Nakayama (1999) log Betti spaces, and Looijenga and others on the boundary of M_g

ideas.what: Interpretation of T_d as π_1 = H_1 of the fibres of the deleted tubular neighbourhood of the stratum
ideas.modern_name: Local fundamental group at the boundary / free abelian group generated by Dehn twists about vanishing cycles
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Picard–Lefschetz); for M_g boundary strata: Harer, Ivanov, Looijenga, Bers
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to the structure at infinity of M_{g,ν} and to tubular neighbourhoods, without this formalism

missed.claim: This is an unpublished algebro-analytic formalism of 'tubes at infinity' for moduli spaces. It uses the twisted torus G_d over the normalized stratum and (next page) a G_d-torsor P_d modelling the punctured normal bundle. It anticipates the log-geometric / Kato–Nakayama description of the boundary of M̄_{g,n}, which was developed independently later.
missed.quote: T_d s'interprètent en termes de S_d comme un syst. local des π_1 en H_1 des fibres
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical. It shows Grothendieck setting up, around the time of the Esquisse, the same tube/torus data later used for log structures on M̄_{g,n} and for tangential base points in Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory. Mathematically it is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The constructions are standard in content (Deligne's normalized multiple loci with sign systems; tori of Dehn multitwists; the punctured normal bundle as a torus torsor). The only interest is the historical one of seeing Grothendieck's intrinsic set-up for the structure at infinity of M_{g,ν}.
transcription_corrections: Line 4: probably 'soit l'intersection des germes D_x^i, et/ou[?] aussi que...'. The superscript 'et/ou' above the comma is likely 'et' with a correction mark.
'X = D_0 ≃ E^2': E is likely a blackboard/script E (affine or Euclidean plane 𝔼^2).
'D_1 = lieu courbe (normalisation de la courbe tracée)': 'lieu' replaces a crossed-out word, and the bracket '(normalisation de la courbe tracée)' annotates D_1.
In (184), 'G_m' is written as a blackboard G_m with subscript D_d. The right-hand side is D_d^! ∧^{(S_d)_{D_d}} G_m^d.
Last line: '[...] et T_d s'interprètent en termes de G_d comme un syst. local des π_1 ou H_1 des fibres'. It is likely 'ou H_1', not 'en H_1', and possibly 'G_d' rather than 'S_d'.
